answers.answer: Separate Conflict cards by I/II/III backs. Shuffle all four III onto the bottom, deal five shuffled II on top, then one shuffled I on top: 10 total (1 I, 5 II, 4 III). Return unused cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup: 10-card Conflict Deck, 1 I, 5 II, 4 III; return unused cards to box without looking.

answers.answer: Four-player human starts at 1 VP; three-player at 0 VP. In both, two Agents are on the Leader and the third beside the board; of 12 troop cubes, 3 go in garrison and 9 in supply; take 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: Score marker on 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader, third next to board; three troops in garrison, remaining nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: You may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take a later Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from your remaining hand, not Agent-played cards. Clean Up moves all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn structure: Agent turns are optional; after Reveal your turns are skipped. Reveal resolves just-revealed cards only; Clean Up moves all cards in front to discard.

answers.answer: No: entry cost is paid before resolving space or card effects, so the Agent-box effect cannot pay that entry. One card sends one Agent using one matching icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn; it may be revealed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs before effects; one card cannot send multiple Agents; card with no Agent icons may only be revealed.

answers.answer: At a Combat space deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison, five total. At a non-Combat space you cannot normally deploy, and recruited troops stay in garrison. Recruit from supply into garrison.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruit from supply to garrison; at Combat deploy any/all troops recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison.

answers.answer: Spy Agent icon lets an Agent visit a space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling it; the played card must still have that icon. Infiltrate recalls a Spy connected to another player's occupied destination to bypass that Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy connected to the visited space to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing the Agent and before effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both.
answers.evidence: Spies: Spy Agent access needs no recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent; Gather Intelligence is chosen after placement before effects; same Spy cannot pay both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four swords 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit, you cannot play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, revealed sword 1; last unit removed means strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes, passing once does not prevent playing later. The window closes when all players involved pass consecutively, then Combat resolves using adjusted strength. After rewards, troops go to supply, not garrison, and sandworms return to bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: not required to pass just because passed earlier; resolve after consecutive passes. Cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: In four players, two tied first each take the second reward; remaining players compete for third and nobody takes the Conflict card. In three players, two tied first each take second reward, no other rewards, and nobody takes the card. Zero strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: exactly two tied first in 4 players lets others compete for third; with 3 or fewer no other rewards; nobody takes card. Zero strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Control and battle icons on Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a 3-spice-for-1-VP option you may pay 3 for 1 VP or 6 for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms double; control and battle icons excluded; optional cost can be paid again, example 3 spice/1 VP or 6/2.

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card face up, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply. A match is mandatory: flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any of the three battle icons in your supply and scores 1 VP for the pair.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: on winning check face-up Conflict or Objective; must flip a matching pair for 1 VP; at Endgame wild may match any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence gain 1 VP; falling below loses it, and returning to 2 earns it again. At 4 gain the printed track bonus, retained below 4 and earned again on return. First to 4 also gains Alliance and its 1 VP, temporary while held. Tying the holder does not take it; rising above does, subject to FAQ holder-loses-Influence transfer.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: VP at 2 reversible below; 4 track bonus retained; first to 4 gains Alliance +1 VP; tie does not steal, rising above transfers.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. Pool multiple sources for one card or split one source among cards. The Row refills to five, and you can buy a replacement immediately if affordable. Acquired cards go face up to discard; unused Persuasion is lost.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: Reveal timing, pool/split, Row replacement can be bought, acquired card to discard; unused Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: During Makers, add 1 spice to an unoccupied Maker space's bonus spot, accumulating; a visitor gains all bonus spice even if choosing worms. Hooks are required only when summoning effect specifies them, and are retained, not spent. The Shield Wall blocks worms at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin; once removed worms may be summoned to any Conflict. A worm is never placed in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers and Sandworms: add bonus at unoccupied Maker spaces; visit gains all; Hooks not universal and not spent; Shield Wall protects three locations; removed permits any Conflict; worms never garrisoned.

answers.answer: At Recall at round end, 10+ VP for any player or an empty Conflict deck triggers Endgame. Players may first play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring: end of round trigger, resolve Endgame Intrigue then most VP; tiebreakers spice, Solari, water, garrison troops.

answers.answer: CHOAM starts with 2 of 20 contracts face up and 18 face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue and four Imperium cards to those decks. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box; they are not among the standard 20.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup: 2 face up, 18 face down; add 4 Intrigue and 4 Imperium; Shaddam option. Contrasting-back contracts are separate Rise of Ix compatibility set.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, take one of two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank, face up. If none remain, icon gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes when visiting Maker space and gaining the shown spice amount that turn in total, including other sources; Immediate completes on taking it; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM taking/completing contracts: take and replace; icon reverts to 2 Solari when empty; definitions for Harvest, Immediate and Acquire The Spice Must Flow.

answers.answer: No; you must hold the board-space contract when sending the Agent, so wait for a future turn. On completion announce it, gain its rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Contract completion: if you already sent Agent to named space, wait; must have held contract then. Announce, gain rewards, flip face down and leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives go randomly to humans, and First Player goes to the human whose card shows it. Order is First Player, Rival, other human. Rival never Reveals; it takes Agent turns while Agents remain in supply.
answers.evidence: Required Rival: one shared Rival, Rival gets Ornithopter, first player only between humans, order First Player → Rival → other human; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: Ignore an occupied board destination and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places no Agent: try an empty specified post; if none, ignore placement; either way reveal another card and continue. Ignore normal space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied means reveal again; Place Spy never sends Agent and reveals another; ignore normal space costs/effects; empty deck or Reshuffle reshuffle and continue.

answers.answer: Remove Objective cards with player-count markings that do not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and each human draws one at random face up. The human with the First Player marker on their Objective takes First Player. Shaddam cannot be chosen without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup: omit mismatched Objective markings, each draws one randomly, marker determines First Player; do not use Shaddam unless CHOAM.

answers.answer: Bank Solari, spice, water and sandworms are not limited; substitute conveniently if depleted. If personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until some troops return there. Take gains from bank and return resource payments to bank.
answers.evidence: Setup bank: not meant to be limited, substitute; gains from bank, payments return. Recruitment stops if supply is empty.

answers.answer: Phases: Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal top Conflict card and each player draws five from own deck. At Recall, if no Endgame, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise and begin next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists five phases; Round Start reveals Conflict and draws five; Recall if no winner returns Agents, passes marker and starts round.

answers.answer: Yes, space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence may be resolved in any order. No, the visit's Influence cannot satisfy entry: costs and requirements must be met before any effects resolve.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay cost and meet requirements before effects; space and Agent-box effects and Faction advance may be done in any order.

answers.answer: No, an arrow cost/effect can be used only once per turn, except sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory; exceptions include may, optional arrow costs and black-X trash. Direct self-trash is mandatory, and Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows: once per turn except doubled Conflict rewards. FAQ: most effects mandatory; may, arrows and black-X optional; direct self-trash mandatory; Intrigue conditions/costs required.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If none in supply, you may first recall a Spy for no effect. If the effect specifies a required Agent-icon type connected to the post, you must place at a post matching it or cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Spy placement rules: unoccupied post; may recall one from post if none in supply; some effects require a particular Agent icon connected to post.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. A Spy does not allow an Agent turn without playing a card; recall still requires a card and does not waive costs or requirements. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement; one may be used for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spy rules: cannot bypass own Agent; FAQ says recall requires played card and does not waive costs; never two Gather Intelligence recalls on same placement.

answers.answer: Controller receives the separate visit bonus from any visitor, including themself: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Conflict winner places/replaces the Control marker. When its Conflict is revealed, controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations: controller bonus on any visit; winner replaces marker; defensive troop comes from supply. Board guide says visitor and controller effects are separate.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets third reward; winner keeps first reward and Conflict card, with no further rewards. Tie for third gets nothing. If three tie for first in a four-player game, each tied player gets second reward, no other rewards, and nobody takes the card.
answers.evidence: Combat ties table specifies tie-second, tie-third, and 3+ first tie in four-player games.

answers.answer: With three players at three different positive strengths, first and second get rewards and third gets nothing. A Rival is a competitor in the 2-human game, so ordinary 2–3 player ranks apply; third reward is used only for a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Combat rewards: 2 or 3 players first/second rewarded, ordinary third gets nothing; third reward only for second-place tie.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue is playable during your Agent or Reveal turn; Combat only during Combat; Endgame only at game end. Keep unplayed cards face down, separate from deck; resolved Intrigues go face up in discard by Intrigue Deck. If its deck empties, shuffle discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue rules specify timing and face-down holding/face-up discard; FAQ says shuffle Intrigue discard if deck runs out.

answers.answer: Ordinary discard is a card of your choice from hand, not in play or discard pile, and cannot be Intrigue unless stated. Secrets takes one randomly selected Intrigue from each opponent with at least four.
answers.evidence: Discarding section specifies hand and excludes Intrigue unless specified; Secrets steals randomly from each opponent with 4+.

answers.answer: Trash may remove a card from hand, discard pile or in play. Ordinary cards return to box; Reserve cards return to Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless a cost or direct self-trash requires it. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP remains even if card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing rules specify locations, destinations and optionality; FAQ Victory says acquired Spice Must Flow VP is retained if trashed.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once upon acquiring a card. When deck is empty and you need to draw, shuffle discard into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at end of Reveal and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box resolves at acquisition; empty deck reshuffles discard; Persuasion cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Agent-played and Reveal cards remain in play until Clean Up, unless trashed. Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of order played if each has another Fremen card in play; they leave play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: both sets of cards remain until Clean Up; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents, not the one placed this turn; it can be used again on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves troop from Conflict to garrison. Retreat any number may mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent returns another Agent and may reuse this round; Retreat moves troop to garrison; FAQ says retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A freely chosen gain of two Influence must be placed in one Faction, not split. Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance; minimum-Influence effect requires the stated minimum with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence rules: free-choice two cannot choose two different Factions; Alliance icon requires token; some effects require minimum Influence.

answers.answer: If holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes Alliance; if several were tied, the former holder chooses recipient. If holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return Alliance to board and former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Official FAQ Alliance loss states transfer after holder loses Influence and return to board at 3 or lower if nobody has 4+.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, then you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up, is used at Reveal, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing specifies during-Reveal use, after-Reveal carry to next round plus five, and delayed Plot Reveal effect then discard.

answers.answer: No, a win-triggered Intrigue cannot be played after a tie for first. If received as a reward for an outright Conflict win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops: cannot play 'when you win' after tying; if received for winning, may play immediately.

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the most recent player to take a Reveal turn wins. Scores can exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ Victory: remaining tie breaks by most recent Reveal; scores may exceed printed track's 12.

answers.answer: No, fulfill all held contracts for the same space with that one Agent placement. Contract is another Agent-turn effect and may resolve in any order with space/card effects, but you must hold it when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion: all same-space contracts with one placement; resolve as another effect in any order; must hold at placement.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. His Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring. His Signet Ring deployment restriction begins immediately when the Agent is sent and lasts only that turn, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ Shaddam: set-aside contracts do not start possessed, may choose when acquiring; Signet restriction immediate and only for turn.

answers.answer: Feyd token starts on the leftmost Training track space and stays on the rightmost once reached. Lady Jessica side begins face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications for Feyd and Lady Jessica; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica can act on flip turn.

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 even with multiple Influence gained. You may reach 2 again after losing and regaining Influence; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor to discard does not trigger its discard ability; discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications specify passing 2 while gaining multiple, reaching again only while moving up; Spacing Guild's Favor Clean Up does not trigger.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access, draws a card and lets you take a contract with CHOAM; without CHOAM or if none remain, it gives 2 Solari. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, gives 1 Emperor Influence and a contract or 2 Solari under those same conditions. No automatic Faction gain comes from either space's access icon; Dutiful's 1 Emperor Influence is explicitly listed.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide lists Accept Contract (Spice Trade) effects and Dutiful Service (Emperor) +1 Influence; guide clarifies non-Faction spaces do not grant automatic Influence, and faction gain is once total.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, controller separately gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries give access, costs, Combat labels and effects for Arrakeen, Fremkit and Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or two sandworms with Maker Hooks. Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or one worm with Hooks. Both options gain all accumulated bonus spice; Hooks are retained, not spent. Shield Wall blocks summoning at the three protected locations.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide lists costs/base/worm choices; Maker rules grant all bonus spice; Hooks never spent; Shield Wall restricts three locations.

answers.answer: Both options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Hooks if lacking them, recruit a troop and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove Shield Wall; no troop is included.
answers.evidence: Sietch Tabr row: no resource cost, 2+ Fremen; choose Hooks if lacking + recruit + water, or water + optional Wall removal.

answers.answer: Both visits cost 5 Solari; High Council is not Combat. First visit places Councilor on an unoccupied seat and grants 2 Persuasion on every Reveal for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits gain 2 spice, draw Intrigue and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: High Council board-space entry lists cost, first visit and subsequent visits; no Combat label.

answers.answer: Costs 8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster, 6 afterward. Each player may take it once per game; take the third Agent, usable this round and thereafter. A Rival obtaining Swordmaster also lowers human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Swordmaster row gives 8/6 cost, once per player, immediate availability; Rival gain lowers human cost.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, costs 3 Solari. You may discard an Intrigue to draw one; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It grants no Emperor Influence and cannot recall the newly placed Agent.
answers.evidence: Imperial Privilege entry states icon/requirement/cost/effects; Landsraad is not a Faction; Recall Agent returns another Agent.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Guild Influence, costs 3 spice, and gives 5 Solari plus 1 Influence with any one Faction. The free-choice Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Shipping entry: 3 spice; 2+ Guild; 5 Solari and Influence with any one Faction.

answers.answer: Gather Support (Landsraad, noncombat) lets you recruit two troops for free or pay 2 Solari and also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery (City, Combat) gives 2 Solari free or 4 Solari for 1 spice; controller separately gets 1 Solari on a visit.
answers.evidence: Board-space rows list Gather Support and Spice Refinery options/status; controlled-location bonus specifies Refinery controller gains Solari.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, 5 spice, +1 Guild Influence, five troops, Combat. Desert Tactics: Fremen, 1 water, +1 Fremen Influence, one troop, optional trash, Combat. Sardaukar: Emperor, 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, Intrigue and four troops, not Combat. Heighliner and Desert Tactics permit normal deployment.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows show costs/effects and Combat labels; Combat spaces permit normal deployment.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall (Landsraad, no cost) draws Intrigue and grants 1 Persuasion during Reveal if your Agent remains there. Espionage (Bene Gesserit, 1 spice) grants 1 Influence, draws a card and places a Spy. Deliver Supplies (Spacing Guild, no cost) grants 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows list each icon, cost and effect including Assembly Hall Reveal condition.

answers.answer: Affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. False Orders can be played without an opposing Spy connected there. Litany Against Fear red box is ignored during Reveal or when it gains an Agent icon and is played as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ False Orders and Litany Against Fear rulings specify all three clauses.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You can acquire it by other means but get no 1-Persuasion discount. If not acquired by end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate ruling states no opponent acquisition, your other-means acquisition without discount, and removal after next Reveal.

answers.answer: Rival starts with a color, four bottom-track cubes, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside board, three Spies and 1 water; score/combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining 2P Reshuffle. Its 10 VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Setup lists pieces, water and markers, and retaining 2P Reshuffle; scoring Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame.

answers.answer: When combined Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water equal its printed Swordmaster threshold, spend that amount and take third Agent, usable this round. Spend Solari, then spice, Intrigue, water; retain leftovers. Each unit/card counts as one.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster specifies threshold, combined count, resource priority, leftovers and current-round use.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, spend each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards or 3 water for 1 VP. No, a mixed total of seven does not make one of these specified sets.
answers.evidence: Rival resource VP rule enumerates sets: 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue or 3 water.

answers.answer: Choose the least-Influence Faction; break ties by leftmost priority. Rival gains/losses Influence VP and Alliances like a human, but does not get the resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival rules specify least Influence and leftmost tie break, human-like Influence VP/Alliance, no 4-Influence resource bonus, and numbered icon meaning.

answers.answer: No. On a two-destination card, select only the condition-matching destination; if occupied, reveal another card rather than use the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns specifies one matching destination, occupied behavior and both destination conditions.

answers.answer: Yes, at a Combat space deploy up to two available garrison troops even if no troops were newly recruited; newly recruited troops deploy too. At noncombat, recruits go to garrison. Missing a conditional 2+ Influence bonus does not prevent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent rules: at Combat deploy new and up to two garrison troops even without recruitment; elsewhere garrison; conditional bonus not required.

answers.answer: For unspecified post, use first available Faction post in Rival priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls the other two and triggers Scheme. Rival never recalls Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes gives post priority, full-post behavior, third-Spy Scheme and no recall for those effects.

answers.answer: If Scheme recruits before Agent placement and Rival then goes to Combat, those troops deploy that turn. A Place Spy card with no legal post is ignored, then another Hagal card is revealed and the same Agent turn continues.
answers.evidence: Rival Scheme says pre-placement recruits deploy at Combat; Place Spy instructions say reveal another card whether or not placement succeeds.

answers.answer: Rival always collects all accumulated Maker bonus spice. With Hooks and an unprotected Conflict, it summons one worm at Hagga or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice. If it summons none due to no Hooks or Shield Wall protection, it takes base spice: Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4. Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces: always collect bonus; Hooks/permitted Conflict worm choices replace base; if none, base values; hooks token retained.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if Rival has any deployed unit, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have normal Combat Intrigue window and can respond. With no deployed unit it gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: only if deployed unit, add bottom swords; reshuffle/reveal again; then humans have normal Intrigue window.

answers.answer: Yes, Rival gets control bonuses, defensive troop, battle-icon VP and sandworm reward doubling. It always takes optional Conflict VP if able to pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward yields 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat section states normal placement/control/defensive/battle-icon rules and doubling; always take optional VP when payable; never takes contracts and gets 2 Solari.
